title: Isolation and Transplantation of Rat Pancreatic Islets to Treat Diabetes
author: Li, Kong, et al.

steps.title: Sterilize instruments and prepare supplies
steps.instruction: Sterilize surgical scissors, toothed forceps (>10 cm), hemostatic forceps, ophthalmic forceps, and needle holders. Prepare 50 mL tubes, 75 % ethanol, a thermos box with ice, and medical swabs.

steps.title: Prepare buffers and media
steps.instruction: Set water bath to 37 °C and cool a centrifuge rotor for 50 mL tubes to 4 °C. Prepare Neutralization buffer by adding 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin to HBSS; make two 50 mL bottles. Dilute Collagenase P stock (10 U/mL) with HBSS to a working concentration of 1 U/mL and keep on ice. Prepare RPMI‑1640 medium containing 10 % FBS and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Anesthetize rat and perform cervical dislocation
steps.instruction: Place the rat in the induction chamber of an anesthesia machine, confirm lack of response to toe pinching with toothed forceps, then execute cervical dislocation.

steps.title: Expose thoracic vessels and control bleeding
steps.instruction: Secure the rat on a dissection board (limbs up, tail toward operator). Sterilize abdominal skin and area near the xiphisternum with 75 % ethanol. Using hooked forceps, make a 1 cm longitudinal skin incision above the xiphisternum, cut across the diaphragm, insert scissors into the thoracic cavity, and sever the thoracic aorta and inferior vena cava. Insert absorbent paper to control bleeding and replace when saturated.

steps.title: Expose common bile duct and clamp Oddi
steps.instruction: Using hooked forceps, secure skin around the urethra, cut open the abdominal cavity with surgical scissors to reveal intestines, liver, stomach, and spleen. Gently move the liver to expose the common bile duct and portal vein. Identify Oddi’s sphincter at the bile‑duct‑duodenum junction and clamp it together with the duodenum using hemostatic forceps to prevent leakage of perfusion solution.

steps.title: Insert needle and perfuse pancreas with collagenase
steps.instruction: Draw 10 mL Collagenase P work solution into a 20 mL syringe fitted with a 23 G intravenous needle (original 12 G needle removed). Remove air, pre‑cool the syringe and needle on ice. Rotate the rat 180° so the head faces the operator, insert the needle into the common bile duct near the liver, and slowly inject 1 mL of collagenase solution. Confirm flow into the duct, then clamp the needle and bile duct with hemostatic forceps. (Optional: clamp the bile duct near the liver, insert a venous catheter into the duodenum, and perfuse 10 mL.) Critical: use the 23 G needle to avoid rupture of the duct; keep the assembly on ice to preserve enzyme activity.

steps.title: Complete pancreas perfusion
steps.instruction: Continue injecting the remaining collagenase work solution at a steady rate until the pancreas visibly swells and becomes translucent. Gently manipulate the duodenum to ensure perfusion of the pancreatic tail near the spleen. If perfusion is incomplete, aspirate an additional 2 mL collagenase solution and continue until the entire tail is filled. Observe pancreas bulging without withdrawing the needle prematurely.

steps.title: Extract perfused pancreas and place on ice
steps.instruction: Gradually release the hemostatic forceps, withdraw the needle, and observe the inflated pancreas attached to surrounding organs. Detach the pancreas from the colon using smooth forceps, dissect ligaments with ophthalmic forceps, strip the pancreas upward along the intestines, stomach, and spleen, then sever the bile ducts and portal vein. Place the stripped pancreas into a 50 mL tube whose interior walls have been pre‑wetted with cold collagenase solution. The post‑perfusion pancreas volume should be 5–10 mL; avoid squeezing to preserve tissue integrity.

steps.title: Collect pancreases for digestion
steps.instruction: Place the tube containing the pancreas on ice. Repeat the entire perfusion procedure for additional rats, adding each pancreas to the same tube but never more than two pancreases per tube. Begin digestion within 1 h of perfusion completion and keep all samples on ice.

steps.title: Digest pancreas in collagenase at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Add 3–5 mL Collagenase P work solution to fully submerge the pancreas in the 50 mL tube. Incubate the tube in a 37 °C water bath for 30 min.

steps.title: Terminate digestion with cold neutralization buffer
steps.instruction: Immediately transfer the tube to ice and add 25 mL cold Neutralization buffer (12 mL per rat). Shake the tube manually for 15 seconds to halt enzymatic activity.

steps.title: Wash tissue pellet with neutralization buffer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 180 g, 4 °C for 1 min; decant supernatant. Add 25 mL Neutralization buffer, vortex to resuspend, and repeat the addition, shaking, centrifugation, and resuspension two more times for thorough washing.

steps.title: Filter suspension through 425 µm metal strainer
steps.instruction: Steam‑sterilize the metal filter, dry at 65 °C, then pre‑wet with 3 mL Neutralization buffer. Filter the tissue suspension, rinse the filter with an additional 10 mL Neutralization buffer to maximize islet recovery.

steps.title: Centrifuge and drain filtered suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtrate at 180 g, 4 °C for 2 min. Carefully decant supernatant and invert the tube on a paper towel for 5 min to remove excess liquid.

steps.title: Layer tissue with Histopaque 1077
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL Histopaque 1077, vortex until homogeneous, and rinse the tube wall with another 5 mL 1077. Tilt the tube 30° and gently pour 5–10 mL Neutralization buffer along the wall, creating a clear interface between the 1077 and buffer layers.

steps.title: Purify islets by density gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 1750 g, 4 °C for 20 min using minimum acceleration and no braking. This separates the suspension into three layers, with islets residing in the middle layer as a visible pellet.

steps.title: Collect islet middle layer and wash
steps.instruction: Aspirate as much of the islet pellet from the middle layer as possible into a tube containing 20 mL Neutralization buffer. Centrifuge at 180 g, 4 °C for 1 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 20 mL Neutralization buffer, vortex, and repeat this wash three times to remove residual 1077.

steps.title: Resuspend purified islets in culture medium
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in 5 mL RPMI‑1640 medium with 10 % FBS. Transfer the suspension to a 60 mm non‑treated petri dish and rinse the tube walls with an additional 5 mL medium, adding all liquid to the dish.

steps.title: Hand‑pick islets under stereomicroscope
steps.instruction: Using a bottom‑illuminated stereomicroscope at 40×, hand‑pick islets with a 200 µL pipette gun, avoiding other tissue. Transfer each islet to a 35 mm dish containing 2 mL islet medium and gently blow through the dish to prevent clustering. Ensure dishes are non‑treated or ultra‑low‑attachment.

steps.title: Shake and incubate islets before use
steps.instruction: Place the 35 mm dish on a level surface and gently cross‑shake to evenly distribute islets. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 14–16 h. Keep fewer than 500 islets per dish. For transplantation, select islets 50–225 µm in diameter, round or oval, and free of damage; a 12 h incubation smooths uneven edges.
